 461→    def reconstruct(self, req_id: str) -> Optional[dict[str, Any]]:
 462→        """Everything the ledger says about one request: who asked what, when, through which
 463→        channel; the considered documents (ids, titles, containers); Gate-2 decisions and reason
 464→        codes; what was released and cited; the model; ``answer_ref`` (never the text); reveals."""
 465→        with self._lock:
 466→            evs = self._db.execute("SELECT * FROM events WHERE req_id = ? ORDER BY seq",
 467→                                   (req_id,)).fetchall()
 468→            if not evs:
 469→                return None
 470→            reveals = self._db.execute("SELECT * FROM events WHERE kind = 'audit.reveal' AND "
 471→                                       "target_req_id = ? ORDER BY seq", (req_id,)).fetchall()
 472→            docs = self._docs_of(req_id)
 473→        out: dict[str, Any] = {
 474→            "req_id": req_id, "sub": None, "channel": None, "question": None,
 475→            "question_sha256": None, "event_time": None, "recorded_at": None,
 476→            "synthetic_replay": False, "policy_version": None, "directory_epoch": None,
 477→            "time_window": None, "considered": [], "gate2": [], "released": [], "citations": [],
 478→            "model": None, "prompt_version": None, "answer_ref": None, "answer_sha256": None,
 479→            "refused": None, "latency_ms": None, "dropped_sentences_count": None,
 480→            "failure": None, "status": "in_progress", "reveals": [], "events": []}
 481→        by_doc = {d["doc_id"]: d for d in docs}
 482→        for r in evs:
 483→            d = json.loads(r["data"])
 484→            out["events"].append({"seq": r["seq"], "kind": r["kind"], "hash": r["hash"],
 485→                                  "event_time": r["event_time"], "recorded_at": r["recorded_at"]})
 486→            out["synthetic_replay"] = out["synthetic_replay"] or bool(r["synthetic"])
 487→            out["sub"] = out["sub"] or d.get("sub")
 488→            k = r["kind"]
 489→            if k == "request.accepted":
 490→                out.update(channel=d.get("channel"), question=d.get("question"),
 491→                           question_sha256=d.get("question_sha256"), event_time=r["event_time"],
 492→                           recorded_at=r["recorded_at"], policy_version=d.get("policy_version"),
 493→                           directory_epoch=d.get("directory_epoch"))
 494→            elif k == "retrieval.decided":
 495→                out["time_window"] = d.get("time_window")
 496→                out["gate1_policy_version"] = d.get("gate1_policy_version")
 497→                out["considered"] = [by_doc.get(x, {"doc_id": x}) for x in d.get("considered") or ()]
 498→                out["gate2"] = list(d.get("gate2") or ())
 499→                out["released"] = [{"doc_id": x, "title": by_doc.get(x, {}).get("title"),
 500→                                    "container": by_doc.get(x, {}).get("container")}
 501→                                   for x in d.get("released") or ()]
 502→            elif k == "answer.released":
 503→                out.update(model=d.get("model"), prompt_version=d.get("prompt_version"),
 504→                           answer_ref=d.get("answer_ref"), answer_sha256=d.get("answer_sha256"),
 505→                           refused=d.get("refused"), latency_ms=d.get("latency_ms"),
 506→                           dropped_sentences_count=d.get("dropped_sentences_count"),
 507→                           status="refused" if d.get("refused") else "released")
 508→                out["citations"] = [{**c, "title": by_doc.get(c.get("doc_id"), {}).get("title")}
 509→                                    for c in d.get("citations") or () if isinstance(c, dict)]
 510→            elif k == "request.failed":
 511→                out["failure"] = {"stage": d.get("stage"), "error_code": d.get("error_code")}
 512→                out["status"] = "failed"
 513→            if out["event_time"] is None:
 514→                out["event_time"], out["recorded_at"] = r["event_time"], r["recorded_at"]
 515→        for r in reveals:
 516→            d = json.loads(r["data"])
 517→            out["reveals"].append({"seq": r["seq"], "by": d.get("sub"), "reason": d.get("reason"),
 518→                                   "event_time": r["event_time"], "recorded_at": r["recorded_at"]})
 519→        return out

1→"""Natural-language audit questions -> the closed `AuditFilter` (plan §4.7, ``POST /audit/ask``).
   2→
   3→Deterministic first: keyword and pattern rules compute the filter. A model is OPTIONAL and only
   4→consulted (``llm=``) when the rules recognise nothing; its output must validate as the same closed
   5→schema (``extra="forbid"``) and passes through the same range cap, otherwise the deterministic result
   6→is used. The model is given the question and the clock — never a ledger row.
   7→
   8→Examples (``now`` = the estate clock):
   9→
  10→* "Show me everything user `jdoe` accessed related to the `payment-gateway` Confluence space in the
  11→  last 30 days" -> user=jdoe, container=payment-gateway, since=now-30d, until=now
  12→* "who accessed PAY-201" / "who accessed confluence:cf-1001" -> doc=...
  13→* "what did priya.sre ask last week" -> user=priya.sre, kind=request.accepted, previous calendar week
  14→* "denied requests for ken.ext" -> user=ken.ext, decision=deny
  15→
  16→Time phrases: "last|past N hours|days|weeks|months|years", "last week|month" (previous calendar
  17→week/month in the clock's timezone), "this week|month", "today", "yesterday", "since <date>",
  18→"before|until <date>", "between <date> and <date>", "on <date>". No time phrase -> the last 365
  19→days. Every range is capped at 365 days (the earlier end moves; the note says so). Ranges are
  20→half-open, ``since <= event_time < until``: "yesterday" ends at today's midnight, exclusive.
  21→
  22→Fail closed (Codex sec r1 #16/#17). A constraint the question names but that does not validate (a
  23→title with characters outside the closed vocabulary, an impossible date such as 2026-02-30) raises
  24→`NlFilterError` carrying the unparsed constraint; it is never dropped to run a broader query. A
  25→configured model whose output does not validate, or that fails, is an `NlFilterError` too.
  26→"""

 122→def _day(s: str, tz: dt.tzinfo) -> dt.datetime:
 123→    try:
 124→        d = dt.date.fromisoformat(s)
 125→    except ValueError:
 126→        raise NlFilterError(f"{s} is not a valid date", {"date": s}) from None

 134→def parse_time(q: str, now: dt.datetime) -> tuple[Optional[dt.datetime], Optional[dt.datetime], str]:
 135→    """(since, until, matched phrase) — both None when the question names no time."""
 136→    tz = now.tzinfo or dt.timezone.utc
 137→    now = now if now.tzinfo else now.replace(tzinfo=tz)
 138→    midnight = now.replace(hour=0, minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0)
 139→    m = re.search(r"\b(?:last|past|previous)\s+(\d{1,4})\s+(hour|day|week|month|year)s?\b", q, re.I)
 140→    if m:
 141→        # clamp before subtracting (9999 years would leave datetime's range); _cap notes the cap
 142→        span = min(int(m.group(1)) * _UNITS[m.group(2).lower()], 2 * MAX_RANGE)
 143→        return now - span, now, m.group(0)
 144→    m = re.search(rf"\bbetween\s+{_DATE}\s+and\s+{_DATE}\b", q, re.I)
 145→    if m:
 146→        a, b = sorted((_day(m.group(1), tz), _day(m.group(2), tz)))   # order before capping
 147→        return a, b + dt.timedelta(days=1), m.group(0)
 148→    m = re.search(rf"\bon\s+{_DATE}\b", q, re.I)
 149→    if m:
 150→        d = _day(m.group(1), tz)
 151→        return d, d + dt.timedelta(days=1), m.group(0)
 152→    since = until = None
 153→    phrase = []
 154→    m = re.search(rf"\b(?:since|after|from)\s+{_DATE}\b", q, re.I)
 155→    if m:
 156→        since = _day(m.group(1), tz)
 157→        phrase.append(m.group(0))
 158→    m = re.search(rf"\b(?:before|until|till|to)\s+{_DATE}\b", q, re.I)
 159→    if m:
 160→        until = _day(m.group(1), tz) + (dt.timedelta(days=1) if "until" in m.group(0).lower() or
 161→                                         "till" in m.group(0).lower() else dt.timedelta(0))
 162→        phrase.append(m.group(0))
 163→    if phrase:
 164→        return since, until or now, " ".join(phrase)
 165→    week_start = midnight - dt.timedelta(days=midnight.weekday())
 166→    if re.search(r"\b(?:last|previous|past)\s+week\b", q, re.I):
 167→        return week_start - dt.timedelta(weeks=1), week_start, "last week"
 168→    if re.search(r"\bthis\s+week\b", q, re.I):
 169→        return week_start, now, "this week"
 170→    if re.search(r"\b(?:last|previous|past)\s+month\b", q, re.I):
 171→        this_month = _month_start(midnight)
 172→        return _month_start(this_month - dt.timedelta(days=1)), this_month, "last month"
 173→    if re.search(r"\bthis\s+month\b", q, re.I):
 174→        return _month_start(midnight), now, "this month"
 175→    if re.search(r"\b(?:last|past)\s+year\b", q, re.I):
 176→        return now - _UNITS["year"], now, "last year"
 177→    if re.search(r"\byesterday\b", q, re.I):
 178→        return midnight - dt.timedelta(days=1), midnight, "yesterday"
 179→    if re.search(r"\btoday\b", q, re.I):
 180→        return midnight, now, "today"
 181→    return None, None, ""

 184→def _cap(since: Optional[dt.datetime], until: Optional[dt.datetime], now: dt.datetime,
 185→         notes: list[str]) -> tuple[dt.datetime, dt.datetime]:
 186→    until = until or now
 187→    if since is None:
 188→        since = until - MAX_RANGE
 189→        notes.append("no time range named: the last 365 days")
 190→    if since > until:                                    # order first, then cap (Codex sec r1 #17)
 191→        since, until = until, since
 192→        notes.append("the range was given in reverse; its ends were swapped")
 193→    if until - since > MAX_RANGE:
 194→        since = until - MAX_RANGE
 195→        notes.append("range capped at 365 days")
 196→    return since, until

 199→def parse_deterministic(question: str, now: dt.datetime, *, limit: int = 100) -> NlParse:
 200→    q = " ".join(str(question or "").split())
 201→    rec: list[str] = []
 202→    notes: list[str] = []
 203→    user = container = doc = None
 204→
 205→    # documents first: explicit ids, then "who accessed <thing>"
 206→    m = _PLATFORM_DOC.search(q)
 207→    if m:
 208→        doc = m.group(0)
 209→    else:
 210→        m = _JIRA_KEY.search(q)
 211→        if m and not re.search(rf"\b(?:user|for|by)\s+{_Q}{re.escape(m.group(0))}", q, re.I):
 212→            doc = m.group(0)
 213→    w = _WHO_ACCESSED.search(q)
 214→    if w and doc is None:
 215→        target = _TIME_TAIL.sub("", w.group("d")).strip().rstrip("?.!").strip()
 216→        target = re.sub(r"^(?:the|a|an)\s+", "", target, flags=re.I)
 217→        target = re.sub(r"\s+(?:page|doc|document|file|issue|ticket|thread)$", "", target, flags=re.I)
 218→        target = _clean_id(target)
 219→        if target and not re.search(r"\b(?:space|channel|project|drive)\b", target, re.I):
 220→            doc = target[:300]
 221→    if doc:
 222→        rec.append("doc")
 223→
 224→    for p in _CONTAINER_PATTERNS:
 225→        m = p.search(q)
 226→        if m and _clean_id(m.group("c")).lower() not in _STOP:
 227→            container = _clean_id(m.group("c"))
 228→            break
 229→    if container is None and doc is None:
 230→        m = _RELATED.search(q)
 231→        if m and _clean_id(m.group("c")).lower() not in _STOP:
 232→            container = _clean_id(m.group("c"))
 233→    if container:
 234→        rec.append("container")
 235→
 236→    for p in _USER_PATTERNS:
 237→        for m in p.finditer(q):
 238→            cand = _clean_id(m.group("u"))
 239→            if cand and cand.lower() not in _STOP and cand != container and cand != doc \
 240→                    and not _JIRA_KEY.fullmatch(cand):
 241→                user = cand
 242→                break
 243→        if user:
 244→            break
 245→    if user:
 246→        rec.append("user")
 247→
 248→    decision = None
 249→    if _DENY.search(q):
 250→        decision = "deny"
 251→    elif _ALLOW.search(q):
 252→        decision = "allow"
 253→    if decision:
 254→        rec.append("decision")
 255→    kind = None
 256→    for p, k in _KINDS:
 257→        if p.search(q):
 258→            kind = k
 259→            break
 260→    if kind:
 261→        rec.append("kind")
 262→        if kind == "request.failed" and decision == "deny":
 263→            decision = None
 264→
 265→    since, until, phrase = parse_time(q, now)
 266→    if phrase:
 267→        rec.append("time")
 268→    since, until = _cap(since, until, now, notes)
 269→    try:
 270→        f = AuditFilter(user=user, container=container, doc=doc, since=since, until=until,
 271→                        decision=decision, kind=kind, limit=limit)
 272→    except ValidationError:
 273→        # Never drop a named scope to run a broader query (Codex sec r1 #16): name what failed.
 274→        unparsed = {}
 275→        for name, val in (("user", user), ("container", container), ("doc", doc)):
 276→            if val is None:
 277→                continue
 278→            try:
 279→                AuditFilter.model_validate({name: val})
 280→            except ValidationError:
 281→                unparsed[name] = val[:300]
 282→        raise NlFilterError("the question names a constraint that is not a valid filter value; "
 283→                            "nothing was searched", unparsed or {"question": q[:300]}) from None
 284→    return NlParse(filter=f, source="deterministic", notes=notes, recognised=rec)

 287→def _validate_llm(out: Any, now: dt.datetime, limit: int) -> AuditFilter:
 288→    f = out if isinstance(out, AuditFilter) else AuditFilter.model_validate(out)
 289→    notes: list[str] = []
 290→    since, until = _cap(f.since, f.until, now, notes)
 291→    return AuditFilter.model_validate({**f.model_dump(), "since": since, "until": until,
 292→                                       "limit": min(f.limit, limit) if f.limit else limit})

 295→def parse_audit_question(question: str, now: dt.datetime, *, llm: Optional[LlmParser] = None,
 296→                         limit: int = 100) -> NlParse:
 297→    """The closed filter for ``question``. Deterministic rules first; ``llm`` (optional) is asked
 298→    only when they recognise nothing, and its output is validated against the closed schema.
 299→
 300→    Raises `NlFilterError` (never anything else) when the question cannot become a valid filter:
 301→    a named constraint that does not validate, an impossible date, or a configured model whose
 302→    output does not validate or that fails. Nothing broader is substituted."""
 303→    try:
 304→        det = parse_deterministic(question, now, limit=limit)
 305→    except NlFilterError:
 306→        raise
 307→    except Exception:                                                # noqa: BLE001 — 422, not 500
 308→        raise NlFilterError("the question could not be parsed into a filter",
 309→                            {"question": str(question)[:300]}) from None
 310→    if det.recognised or llm is None:
 311→        return det
 312→    try:
 313→        f = _validate_llm(llm(str(question), now), now, limit)
 314→    except Exception:                                                # noqa: BLE001 — any failure
 315→        raise NlFilterError("the rules recognised nothing and the model's filter did not "
 316→                            "validate; nothing was searched",
 317→                            {"question": str(question)[:300]}) from None
 318→    return NlParse(filter=f, source="llm", notes=["filter proposed by the model and validated"],
 319→                   recognised=["llm"])

1→"""``/audit/*`` (CONTRACTS §3): compliance_officer only; every call is itself ledgered.
   2→
   3→* ``GET  /audit/events``                   filter -> event rows        (ledgered ``audit.query``)
   4→* ``GET  /audit/doc/{doc_id}/accessors``   who had a document          (ledgered ``audit.query``)
   5→* ``POST /audit/ask``  {"question"}        NL -> closed filter -> rows (ledgered ``audit.query``)
   6→* ``POST /audit/reveal`` {"req_id","reason"}  the answer text          (ledgered ``audit.reveal``
   7→                                            BEFORE the text is read; a non-empty reason is required)
   8→* ``GET  /audit/verify``                   chain + anchors + external head
   9→
  10→Write-ahead and fail-closed: the audit event is appended before the response is returned; an append
  11→failure is a 503 and nothing is returned. Failed calls are ledgered too (Codex sec r1 #9): an invalid
  12→filter, a blank question or reason, an unparseable question, an unknown reveal target or a query
  13→failure appends ``audit.query`` with ``outcome`` ``rejected``/``error`` before the 4xx/5xx (and is a
  14→503 if that append fails). A reveal whose stored text does not hash to the sealed ``answer_sha256``
  15→returns 409 with no text and is ledgered with ``outcome: mismatch`` (#7). Requests the framework
  16→rejects before a handler runs (no/invalid token, a body that is not JSON or exceeds a length cap) are
  17→not ledgered — they never reach the audit code. The one exception is ``/audit/verify``: its report carries
  18→no content (counts and hashes only) and is exactly what an officer needs when the ledger is broken,
  19→so it is returned with ``"ledgered": false`` when the ledger refuses the ``audit.query`` append.
  20→
  21→``require_role(role)`` comes from the app (auth.py): it returns a FastAPI dependency (a ``Depends``
  22→or a plain callable) that yields the authenticated principal (an object or mapping with ``sub``) and
  23→answers 401/403 itself.
  24→"""
  25→from __future__ import annotations
  26→
  27→import datetime as dt
  28→from typing import Any, Callable, NoReturn, Optional
  29→
  30→from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, Query
  31→from fastapi import params as fa_params
  32→from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
  33→from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, ValidationError
  34→
  35→from ..models import AuditQueryEvent, AuditReveal
  36→from .anchor import AnchorSink
  37→from .anchor import verify as verify_with_sink
  38→from .content import AnswerStore, ContentStoreUnavailable, sha256_text
  39→from .ledger import AccessLedger, LedgerUnavailable
  40→from .nl_filter import LlmParser, NlFilterError, parse_audit_question
  41→from .query import AuditFilter, AuditProjection
  42→
  43→COMPLIANCE_ROLE = "compliance_officer"
  44→REVEAL_MISMATCH = "content does not match the sealed ledger digest"
  45→
  46→
  47→class AuditAskBody(BaseModel):
  48→    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
  49→    question: str = Field(max_length=1000)          # blank -> a ledgered 422 in the handler
  50→
  51→
  52→class RevealBody(BaseModel):
  53→    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
  54→    req_id: str = Field(max_length=200)             # empty -> a ledgered 404 (unknown target)
  55→    reason: str = Field(max_length=1000)            # blank -> a ledgered 422 in the handler
  56→
  57→
  58→def _sub_of(principal: Any) -> str:
  59→    if isinstance(principal, str):
  60→        return principal
  61→    if isinstance(principal, dict):
  62→        sub = principal.get("sub")
  63→    else:
  64→        sub = getattr(principal, "sub", None)
  65→    if not sub:
  66→        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="not authenticated")
  67→    return str(sub)
  68→
  69→
  70→def _unavailable() -> HTTPException:
  71→    return HTTPException(status_code=503, detail={"code": "AUDIT_LEDGER_UNAVAILABLE",
  72→                                                  "message": "the access ledger is unavailable; "
  73→                                                             "nothing was returned"})
  74→
  75→
  76→def make_audit_router(ledger: AccessLedger, store: AnswerStore, projection: AuditProjection,
  77→                      require_role: Callable[[str], Any], *,
  78→                      sink: Optional[AnchorSink] = None,
  79→                      llm: Optional[LlmParser] = None,
  80→                      clock: Optional[Callable[[], dt.datetime]] = None) -> APIRouter:
  81→    dep = require_role(COMPLIANCE_ROLE)
  82→    if not isinstance(dep, fa_params.Depends):
  83→        dep = Depends(dep)
  84→    now = clock or (lambda: dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc))
  85→    router = APIRouter(prefix="/audit", tags=["audit"])
  86→

  89→            ledger.append(AuditQueryEvent(sub=sub, filter=filt, result_count=count,
  90→                                          event_time=now()))
  91→        except LedgerUnavailable:
  92→            raise _unavailable() from None
  93→
  94→    def _ledger_query(sub: str, filt: dict, count: int) -> None:
  95→        _append_query(sub, {**filt, "outcome": "ok"}, count)
  96→
  97→    def _refuse(sub: str, op: str, outcome: str, status: int, error: str,
  98→                info: Optional[dict] = None, detail: Any = None) -> NoReturn:
  99→        """Ledger a failed audit call as ``audit.query`` with ``outcome`` (``rejected`` for a bad
 100→        request, ``error`` for a server-side failure), then answer ``status`` (Codex sec r1 #9).
 101→        When the ledger refuses this append the answer is 503 instead: fail closed."""
 102→        _append_query(sub, {"op": op, "outcome": outcome, **(info or {}), "error": error[:300]}, 0)
 103→        raise HTTPException(status_code=status, detail=error if detail is None else detail)
 104→
 105→    def _sync() -> None:
 106→        try:
 107→            projection.sync()
 108→        except LedgerUnavailable:
 109→            raise _unavailable() from None

 111→    @router.get("/events")
 112→    def audit_events(principal=dep,
 113→                     user: Optional[str] = Query(None), container: Optional[str] = Query(None),
 114→                     doc: Optional[str] = Query(None), since: Optional[str] = Query(None),
 115→                     until: Optional[str] = Query(None),
 116→                     decision: Optional[str] = Query(None), kind: Optional[str] = Query(None),
 117→                     limit: Optional[str] = Query(None)) -> dict:
 118→        # every parameter arrives as text and is validated here, so a malformed one is a
 119→        # ledgered rejection rather than a framework 422 that never reaches the ledger
 120→        sub = _sub_of(principal)
 121→        raw = {k: v for k, v in dict(user=user, container=container, doc=doc, since=since,
 122→                                     until=until, decision=decision, kind=kind,
 123→                                     limit=limit).items() if v is not None}

 125→            f, how = AuditFilter.model_validate(raw).windowed(now())

 176→                      len(rows))

 178→                "notes": parsed.notes, "events": rows}

 181→    def audit_reveal(body: RevealBody, principal=dep) -> Any:
 182→        sub = _sub_of(principal)

 192→        released = None
 193→        for le in evs:
 194→            if le.kind == "answer.released" and le.data.get("req_id") == body.req_id:
 195→                released = le.data
 196→        if released is None or not released.get("answer_ref"):
 197→            _refuse(sub, "reveal", "rejected", 404, "no released answer for that request", info)
 198→        ref, sealed = str(released["answer_ref"]), released.get("answer_sha256")
 199→        try:                                                  # write-ahead: ledger, then read
 200→            ledger.append(AuditReveal(sub=sub, target_req_id=body.req_id, reason=reason,
 201→                                      event_time=now()))
 202→        except LedgerUnavailable:
 203→            raise _unavailable() from None
 204→        try:
 205→            stored = store.get(ref)
 206→        except ContentStoreUnavailable:

 208→        if stored is None:

   3→It is a CACHE of the company's identity source (for the demo: ``world.json``'s ``directory``;
   4→native platforms stay authoritative and Gate 2 asks them). Nested groups are expanded once at load.
   5→Every change bumps ``epoch`` so Gate-1 readable-set caches never survive a directory change.
   6→"""
   7→from __future__ import annotations
   8→
   9→import json
  10→import threading
  11→from pathlib import Path
  12→from typing import Iterable, Optional
  13→
  14→from .models import DirectoryUser, UserKind
  15→
  16→
  17→def _expand_groups(groups: list[dict]) -> dict[str, set[str]]:
  18→    """group id → every user id in it, member_groups expanded transitively (cycle-safe)."""
  19→    direct = {g["id"]: set(g.get("members", [])) for g in groups}
  20→    children = {g["id"]: list(g.get("member_groups", [])) for g in groups}
  21→    out: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
  22→
  23→    def walk(gid: str, seen: frozenset) -> set[str]:
  24→        if gid in out:
  25→            return out[gid]
  26→        if gid in seen:
  27→            return set()
  28→        users = set(direct.get(gid, set()))
  29→        for child in children.get(gid, []):
  30→            users |= walk(child, seen | {gid})
  31→        return users
  32→
  33→    for gid in direct:
  34→        out[gid] = walk(gid, frozenset())
  35→    return out
  36→
  37→
  38→class Directory:
  39→    def __init__(self, users: Iterable[DirectoryUser]) -> None:
  40→        self._lock = threading.Lock()
  41→        self._users: dict[str, DirectoryUser] = {u.id: u for u in users}
  42→        self._by_native: dict[tuple[str, str], str] = {}
  43→        self.epoch = 1
  44→        self._reindex()
  45→
  46→    # -- construction ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  47→    @classmethod
  48→    def from_world(cls, world: dict) -> "Directory":
  49→        d = world.get("directory", {})
  50→        members_of = _expand_groups(d.get("groups", []))
  51→        user_groups: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
  52→        for gid, uids in members_of.items():
  53→            for uid in uids:
  54→                user_groups.setdefault(uid, set()).add(gid)
  55→        users = []
  56→        for u in d.get("users", []):
  57→            groups = set(u.get("groups", [])) | user_groups.get(u["id"], set())
  58→            # a user listed in a child group is also in every ancestor group
  59→            for gid, uids in members_of.items():
  60→                if u["id"] in uids:
  61→                    groups.add(gid)
  62→            users.append(DirectoryUser(
  63→                id=u["id"], name=u.get("name", u["id"]), email=u["email"],
  64→                employment=u.get("employment", "employee"),
  65→                kind=UserKind(u.get("kind", "member")), active=bool(u.get("active", True)),
  66→                roles=tuple(u.get("roles", ["employee"])), groups=tuple(sorted(groups)),
  67→                platform_ids=dict(u.get("platform_ids", {}))))
  68→        return cls(users)
  69→
  70→    @classmethod
  71→    def from_world_file(cls, path: Path) -> "Directory":
  72→        return cls.from_world(json.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8")))
  73→
  74→    def _reindex(self) -> None:
  75→        self._by_native = {(p, nid): u.id for u in self._users.values()
  76→                           for p, nid in u.platform_ids.items()}
  77→
  78→    # -- DirectoryIndex protocol (connectors/_http.py) ------------------------------------------
  79→    def get(self, user_id: str) -> Optional[DirectoryUser]:
  80→        return self._users.get(user_id)
  81→
  82→    def by_platform_id(self, platform: str, native_id: str) -> Optional[DirectoryUser]:
  83→        uid = self._by_native.get((platform, native_id))
  84→        return self._users.get(uid) if uid else None
  85→
  86→    def all(self) -> list[DirectoryUser]:
  87→        return list(self._users.values())
  88→
  89→    # -- mutation (webhook user.changed / admin) ------------------------------------------------
  90→    def set_active(self, user_id: str, active: bool) -> None:
  91→        with self._lock:
  92→            u = self._users.get(user_id)
  93→            if u is None or u.active == active:
  94→                return
  95→            self._users[user_id] = u.model_copy(update={"active": active})
  96→            self.epoch += 1
  97→

1→"""The Internal Brain's own retrieval index — Gate 1 lives here (plan §4.2 steps 4–5).
   2→
   3→Why its own index rather than Walnut's passage stores (Opus review B2/H6): ranking must not depend
   4→on content the asker cannot read. Here every statistic is computed over the PERMITTED corpus only:
   5→
   6→* BM25 is evaluated in Python with document frequency, corpus size and average length taken from
   7→  the asker's readable chunks — a restricted document changes no permitted passage's score;
   8→* vector similarity is per-chunk cosine (no store routing, no centroids);
   9→* the exact-identifier bonus and the time-window boost read only the candidate chunk.
  10→
  11→So the differential test (P2: same query, world with vs without restricted docs) can hold exactly.
  12→ACLs are policy expressions stored per document and evaluated at query time against the principal
  13→(``acl.allows``); they are mutable without republishing anything (plan §4.3).
  14→"""
  15→from __future__ import annotations
  16→
  17→import json
  18→import math
  19→import re
  20→import sqlite3
  21→import threading
  22→from dataclasses import dataclass
  23→from datetime import datetime
  24→from pathlib import Path
  25→from typing import Callable, Iterable, Optional, Sequence
  26→
  27→import numpy as np
  28→
  29→from . import acl as aclmod
  30→from .models import AclExpr, DirectoryUser, SourceDoc
  31→from .timewin import Window, overlaps
  32→
  33→RRF_K = 60
  34→EXACT_BONUS = 1.0
  35→WINDOW_BONUS = 0.15
  36→TITLE_WEIGHT = 0.6
  37→#: a passage is RELEVANT only if it covers this share of the question's IDF-weighted terms
  38→#: (IDF from the asker's permitted corpus — P2 holds); below it the passage never reaches a model
  39→MIN_COVERAGE = 0.4
  40→MIN_COVERAGE_SINGLE = 0.5
  41→#: without a matching adjacent term pair (e.g. "key rotation"), a clause of ≥3 terms needs this much
  42→MIN_COVERAGE_NO_PHRASE = 0.6
  43→#: weight of the vector leg; the offline hashing embedding is lexical noise, so it barely counts
  44→VECTOR_WEIGHT_REAL, VECTOR_WEIGHT_OFFLINE = 0.35, 0.05
  45→CHUNK_CHARS = 700
  46→BM25_K1, BM25_B = 1.2, 0.75
  47→
  48→_TOKEN = re.compile(r"[a-z0-9]+(?:[-_.][a-z0-9]+)*")
  49→_IDENT = re.compile(r"\b[A-Za-z]{2,10}-\d+\b|\b(?=[A-Za-z0-9-]*\d)(?=[A-Za-z0-9-]*[A-Za-z])[A-Za-z0-9]+(?:-[A-Za-z0-9]+)+\b")
  50→STOPWORDS = frozenset(
  51→    "a an and are as at be been but by can could did do does for from had has have how i if in "
  52→    "into is it its me my of on or our so than that the their them then there these they this to "
  53→    "was we were what when where which who why will with would you your about any there's what's "
  54→    "show tell give find list please latest last week weeks month quarter sprint days day recent "
  55→    "summarize summarise summary explain describe provide link around new current any were".split())
  56→
  57→
  58→#: platform names are routing HINTS (pipeline.platform_hints), not content: "raised in Slack" must
  59→#: not require the word "slack" to appear in a Slack thread
  60→PLATFORM_WORDS = frozenset("slack confluence jira drive google gdrive wiki".split())
  61→_SUFFIXES = ("ing", "ed", "es", "s")
  62→
  63→
  64→def stem(t: str) -> str:
  65→    """Tiny, deterministic suffix stripper (applied identically to docs and queries):
  66→    raised/raise/raising → rais, blockers → blocker."""
  67→    if any(ch.isdigit() for ch in t):
  68→        return t
  69→    for suf in _SUFFIXES:
  70→        if t.endswith(suf) and len(t) - len(suf) >= 4:
  71→            t = t[: -len(suf)]
  72→            break
  73→    if t.endswith("e") and len(t) >= 5:
  74→        t = t[:-1]
  75→    return t
  76→
  77→
  78→def tokens(text: str) -> list[str]:
  79→    out = []
  80→    for t in _TOKEN.findall((text or "").lower()):
  81→        parts = [t] + ([p for p in re.split(r"[-_.]", t) if p] if re.search(r"[-_.]", t) else [])
  82→        for p in parts:
  83→            if len(p) > 1 and p not in STOPWORDS:
  84→                out.append(stem(p))
  85→    return out
  86→
  87→
  88→_CLAUSE = re.compile(r"\band\b|\balso\b|[,;?]|\bplus\b", re.I)
  89→
  90→
  91→def clauses(text: str) -> list[list[str]]:
  92→    """Content terms per clause of a (possibly multi-intent) question."""
  93→    out = [query_terms(c) for c in _CLAUSE.split(text or "")]
  94→    return [c for c in out if c]
  95→
  96→
  97→def query_terms(text: str) -> list[str]:
  98→    plat = {stem(w) for w in PLATFORM_WORDS} | set(PLATFORM_WORDS)
  99→    return [t for t in dict.fromkeys(tokens(text)) if t not in plat]
 100→
 101→
 102→_WORD = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9'-]*")
 103→
 104→
 105→def anchors(text: str) -> set[str]:
 106→    """Distinctive question words: tokens with a digit (Q3, wave-4) or capitalised words that do
 107→    not open the sentence (Indonesian). A clause naming an anchor that occurs in NONE of the asker's
 108→    permitted chunks cannot be answered from their sources."""
 109→    out = set()
 110→    words = _WORD.findall(text or "")
 111→    for i, w in enumerate(words):
 112→        if w.lower() in PLATFORM_WORDS or w in ("I",):
 113→            continue
 114→        if any(ch.isdigit() for ch in w) or (i > 0 and w[0].isupper()):
 115→            out.update(tokens(w))
 116→    return {a for a in out if a not in {stem(p) for p in PLATFORM_WORDS}}
 117→
 118→
 119→def identifiers(text: str) -> list[str]:
 120→    return sorted({m.group(0).upper() for m in _IDENT.finditer(text or "")})
 121→
 122→
 123→def chunk_text(text: str, size: int = CHUNK_CHARS) -> list[str]:
 124→    parts = []
 125→    for p in re.split(r"\n\s*\n|\n", text or ""):
 126→        p = p.strip()
 127→        while len(p) > size:                 # hard limit: split oversized lines (sec1 #33)
 128→            cut = p.rfind(" ", 0, size)
 129→            cut = cut if cut > size // 2 else size
 130→            parts.append(p[:cut].strip())
 131→            p = p[cut:].strip()
 132→        if p:
 133→            parts.append(p)
 134→    out, cur = [], ""
 135→    for p in parts:
 136→        if cur and len(cur) + len(p) + 1 > size:
 137→            out.append(cur)
 138→            cur = p
 139→        else:
 140→            cur = f"{cur}\n{p}" if cur else p
 141→    if cur:
 142→        out.append(cur)
 143→    return out or [""]

 164→class Index:
 165→    def __init__(self, path: Path, *, embedder: Optional[Embedder] = None) -> None:
 166→        self.path = Path(path)
 167→        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
 168→        self.embed = embedder or offline_embedder
 169→        self._lock = threading.RLock()
 170→        self._db = sqlite3.connect(str(self.path), check_same_thread=False)
 171→        self._db.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
 172→        self._db.executescript("""
 173→            PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;
 174→            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS docs(doc_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, platform TEXT, kind TEXT,
 175→                container TEXT, container_name TEXT, title TEXT, version TEXT, created_at TEXT,
 176→                updated_at TEXT, deep_link TEXT, author TEXT, links TEXT, acl TEXT, text TEXT,
 177→                indexed_at TEXT);
 178→            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS chunks(chunk_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, doc_id TEXT, ord INTEGER,
 179→                text TEXT, model TEXT, vec BLOB);
 180→            CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS chunks_doc ON chunks(doc_id);
 181→        """)
 182→        self.acl_version = 0
 183→        self._docs: dict[str, dict] = {}
 184→        self._acl: dict[str, AclExpr] = {}
 185→        self._chunks: dict[str, dict] = {}              # chunk_id -> {doc_id, text, tf, len, vec}
 186→        self._doc_chunks: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
 187→        self._readable_cache: dict[tuple, frozenset[str]] = {}
 188→        self._load()
 189→
 190→    # -- persistence ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 191→    def _load(self) -> None:
 192→        for r in self._db.execute("SELECT * FROM docs"):
 193→            d = dict(r)
 194→            self._docs[d["doc_id"]] = d
 195→            self._acl[d["doc_id"]] = aclmod.parse(d["acl"])
 196→        for r in self._db.execute("SELECT chunk_id, doc_id, text, vec FROM chunks ORDER BY doc_id, ord"):
 197→            vec = np.frombuffer(r["vec"], dtype=np.float32) if r["vec"] else None
 198→            self._add_chunk(r["chunk_id"], r["doc_id"], r["text"], vec)
 199→        self.acl_version += 1
 200→
 201→    def _add_chunk(self, cid: str, doc_id: str, text: str, vec) -> None:
 202→        row = self._docs.get(doc_id, {})
 203→        title = row.get("title", "")
 204→        #: the container (space / project / channel / drive) name is part of a doc's "title" signal
 205→        heading = f"{title} {row.get('container_name', '')}"
 206→        toks = tokens(f"{title}\n{text}")
 207→        tf: dict[str, int] = {}
 208→        for t in toks:
 209→            tf[t] = tf.get(t, 0) + 1
 210→        if vec is not None:
 211→            n = float(np.linalg.norm(vec))
 212→            vec = vec / n if n else vec
 213→        seq = tokens(heading) + ["‖"] + tokens(text)          # ‖ separates heading and body
 214→        pairs = {(a, b) for a, b in zip(seq, seq[1:])}
 215→        self._chunks[cid] = {"doc_id": doc_id, "text": text, "tf": tf, "len": max(1, len(toks)),
 216→                             "pairs": pairs,
 217→                             "vec": vec, "idents": set(identifiers(f"{title} {text}")),
 218→                             "title_terms": set(tokens(heading))}
 219→        self._doc_chunks.setdefault(doc_id, []).append(cid)
 220→
 221→    # -- writes ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 222→    def upsert(self, doc: SourceDoc, acl: AclExpr) -> None:
 223→        pieces = chunk_text(doc.text)
 224→        vecs, model = self.embed([f"{doc.title}\n{p}" for p in pieces])
 225→        now = datetime.now().astimezone().isoformat()
 226→        with self._lock:
 227→            self._drop_doc_locked(doc.doc_id)
 228→            row = {"doc_id": doc.doc_id, "platform": doc.platform, "kind": doc.kind,
 229→                   "container": doc.container, "container_name": doc.container_name,
 230→                   "title": doc.title, "version": doc.version,
 231→                   "created_at": doc.created_at.isoformat(), "updated_at": doc.updated_at.isoformat(),
 232→                   "deep_link": doc.deep_link, "author": doc.author or "",
 233→                   "links": json.dumps(list(doc.links)), "acl": aclmod.dump(acl), "text": doc.text,
 234→                   "indexed_at": now}
 235→            self._db.execute(f"INSERT INTO docs({','.join(row)}) VALUES({','.join('?' * len(row))})",
 236→                             list(row.values()))
 237→            self._docs[doc.doc_id] = row
 238→            self._acl[doc.doc_id] = acl
 239→            for i, (p, v) in enumerate(zip(pieces, vecs)):
 240→                cid = f"{doc.doc_id}#{i}"
 241→                arr = np.asarray(v, dtype=np.float32)
 242→                self._db.execute("INSERT INTO chunks VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?)",
 243→                                 (cid, doc.doc_id, i, p, model, arr.tobytes()))
 244→                self._add_chunk(cid, doc.doc_id, p, arr)
 245→            self._db.commit()
 246→            self._bump()
 247→
 248→    def set_acl(self, doc_id: str, acl: AclExpr) -> None:
 249→        with self._lock:
 250→            if doc_id not in self._docs:
 251→                return
 252→            self._acl[doc_id] = acl
 253→            self._docs[doc_id]["acl"] = aclmod.dump(acl)
 254→            self._db.execute("UPDATE docs SET acl=? WHERE doc_id=?", (aclmod.dump(acl), doc_id))
 255→            self._db.commit()
 256→            self._bump()
 257→
 258→    def delete(self, doc_id: str) -> None:
 259→        with self._lock:
 260→            self._drop_doc_locked(doc_id)
 261→            self._db.commit()
 262→            self._bump()
 263→
 264→    def _drop_doc_locked(self, doc_id: str) -> None:
 265→        for cid in self._doc_chunks.pop(doc_id, []):
 266→            self._chunks.pop(cid, None)
 267→        self._docs.pop(doc_id, None)
 268→        self._acl.pop(doc_id, None)
 269→        self._db.execute("DELETE FROM chunks WHERE doc_id=?", (doc_id,))
 270→        self._db.execute("DELETE FROM docs WHERE doc_id=?", (doc_id,))
 271→
 272→    def _bump(self) -> None:
 273→        self.acl_version += 1
 274→        self._readable_cache.clear()
 275→
 276→    # -- reads ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 277→    def doc(self, doc_id: str) -> Optional[dict]:
 278→        return self._docs.get(doc_id)
 279→
 280→    def doc_ids(self) -> list[str]:
 281→        return list(self._docs)
 282→
 283→    def docs_in_container(self, platform: str, container: str) -> list[str]:
 284→        return [d for d, r in self._docs.items() if r["platform"] == platform and r["container"] == container]
 285→
 286→    def acl_of(self, doc_id: str) -> Optional[AclExpr]:
 287→        return self._acl.get(doc_id)
 288→
 289→    def readable(self, user: DirectoryUser, directory_epoch: int = 0) -> frozenset[str]:
 290→        """GATE 1: every doc whose stored policy admits ``user``. Fail-closed (unknown ⇒ no)."""
 291→        key = (user.id, user.active, user.kind, user.groups, user.email, directory_epoch,
 292→               self.acl_version)
 293→        hit = self._readable_cache.get(key)
 294→        if hit is not None:
 295→            return hit
 296→        with self._lock:
 297→            out = frozenset(d for d, e in self._acl.items() if aclmod.allows(e, user))
 298→            self._readable_cache[key] = out
 299→            return out
 300→
 301→    def search(self, query: str, allowed: Iterable[str], *, k: int = 12,
 302→               window: Optional[Window] = None, relevant_only: bool = False) -> list[Hit]:
 303→        """Hybrid ranking over the PERMITTED chunks only. Restricted chunks are never scored."""
 304→        allowed = set(allowed)
 305→        with self._lock:
 306→            cands = [(cid, c) for d in sorted(allowed) for cid in self._doc_chunks.get(d, [])
 307→                     for c in (self._chunks.get(cid),) if c is not None]
 308→        if not cands:
 309→            return []
 310→        q_terms = query_terms(query)
 311→        q_idents = set(identifiers(query))
 312→        # statistics from the permitted corpus only (P2)
 313→        n = len(cands)
 314→        avgdl = sum(c["len"] for _, c in cands) / n
 315→        df = {t: sum(1 for _, c in cands if t in c["tf"]) for t in q_terms}
 316→        idf = {t: math.log(1 + (n - df[t] + 0.5) / (df[t] + 0.5)) for t in q_terms}
 317→        parts = [c for c in clauses(query) if any(t in idf for t in c)] or [q_terms]
 318→        # A clause naming a distinctive anchor (Q7, Indonesian) that occurs in NONE of the asker's
 319→        # permitted chunks cannot be answered from their sources: it scores 0. df is over the
 320→        # permitted corpus only, so this reveals nothing about restricted content.
 321→        anc = anchors(query)
 322→        answerable = [p for p in parts if not any(t in anc and df.get(t, 0) == 0 for t in p)]
 323→        lex: dict[str, float] = {}
 324→        cover: dict[str, float] = {}
 325→        for cid, c in cands:
 326→            s = 0.0
 327→            hit_terms = set()
 328→            for t in q_terms:
 329→                f = c["tf"].get(t, 0)
 330→                in_title = t in c["title_terms"]
 331→                if f:
 332→                    s += idf[t] * f * (BM25_K1 + 1) / (f + BM25_K1 * (1 - BM25_B + BM25_B * c["len"] / avgdl))
 333→                if in_title:
 334→                    s += TITLE_WEIGHT * idf[t]
 335→                if f or in_title:
 336→                    hit_terms.add(t)
 337→            if s > 0:
 338→                lex[cid] = s
 339→                # best coverage over the question's clauses (multi-intent questions)
 340→                best = 0.0
 341→                for p in answerable:
 342→                    cov = (sum(idf.get(t, 0) for t in p if t in hit_terms) /
 343→                           (sum(idf.get(t, 0) for t in p) or 1.0))
 344→                    phrase = len(p) <= 2 or any(pair in c["pairs"] for pair in zip(p, p[1:]))
 345→                    if not phrase and cov < MIN_COVERAGE_NO_PHRASE:
 346→                        cov = min(cov, MIN_COVERAGE - 0.01)      # cannot pass the gate on scatter
 347→                    best = max(best, cov)
 348→                cover[cid] = best
 349→        max_lex = max(lex.values(), default=0.0) or 1.0
 350→        # vector leg (per-chunk cosine; no routing, no centroids)
 351→        vec_scores: dict[str, float] = {}
 352→        qv, model = self.embed([query])
 353→        w_vec = VECTOR_WEIGHT_OFFLINE if "hash" in str(model).lower() or "offline" in str(model).lower()             else VECTOR_WEIGHT_REAL
 354→        q = np.asarray(qv[0], dtype=np.float32)
 355→        qn = float(np.linalg.norm(q))
 356→        if qn:
 357→            q = q / qn
 358→            for cid, c in cands:
 359→                if c["vec"] is not None and c["vec"].shape == q.shape:
 360→                    vec_scores[cid] = max(0.0, float(np.dot(c["vec"], q)))
 361→        hits = []
 362→        for cid, c in cands:
 363→            l = lex.get(cid, 0.0) / max_lex
 364→            v = vec_scores.get(cid, 0.0)
 365→            exact = q_idents & c["idents"]
 366→            if not l and not exact and v < 0.2:
 367→                continue
 368→            sc = l + w_vec * v + EXACT_BONUS * len(exact)
 369→            d = self._docs.get(c["doc_id"]) if window is not None else None
 370→            if d is not None:
 371→                if overlaps(window, datetime.fromisoformat(d["created_at"]),
 372→                            datetime.fromisoformat(d["updated_at"])):
 373→                    sc += WINDOW_BONUS
 374→            cov = cover.get(cid, 0.0)
 375→            # single-intent questions need half their weighted terms; multi-intent clauses are
 376→            # shorter, so each needs less (a passage answering one part of a two-part question)

 153→        except httpx.HTTPError as exc:                              # transport / timeout

 219→class WebhookVerifier:
 220→    """Signature (over timestamp + delivery id + body) + ±300 s window + replayed-delivery set.
 221→    Thread-safe; replay memory is bounded to ids whose timestamps are still inside the window
 222→    (older ones fail the window check anyway). The set is PER PROCESS: multi-worker / restart replay
 223→    inside the window is a documented limitation (SECURITY.md, track 3 disposition)."""
 224→
 225→    def __init__(self, secret: str, *, window_s: int = WEBHOOK_WINDOW_S,
 226→                 now: Callable[[], float] = time.time):
 227→        if not secret:
 228→            raise ValueError("webhook secret is required")
 229→        self._secret = secret
 230→        self._window = window_s
 231→        self._now = now
 232→        self._seen: dict[str, float] = {}
 233→        self._lock = threading.Lock()

 235→    def verify(self, headers: Mapping[str, str], body: bytes) -> tuple[str, int]:
 236→        delivery = _header(headers, "X-IB-Delivery").strip()
 237→        ts_raw = _header(headers, "X-IB-Timestamp").strip()
 238→        sig = _header(headers, "X-IB-Signature").strip()
 239→        if not delivery or not ts_raw or not sig:
 240→            raise WebhookRejected("missing signature headers")
 241→        try:
 242→            ts = int(ts_raw)
 243→        except ValueError as exc:
 244→            raise WebhookRejected("bad timestamp") from exc
 245→        expected = sign_webhook(self._secret, ts_raw, delivery, body)
 246→        if not hmac.compare_digest(expected.encode(), sig.encode()):
 247→            raise WebhookRejected("bad signature")
 248→        now = self._now()
 249→        if abs(now - ts) > self._window:
 250→            raise WebhookRejected("stale timestamp")
 251→        with self._lock:
 252→            for d, seen_ts in list(self._seen.items()):
 253→                if now - seen_ts > 2 * self._window:
 254→                    del self._seen[d]
 255→            if delivery in self._seen:
 256→                raise WebhookRejected("replayed delivery")
 257→            self._seen[delivery] = float(ts)
 258→        return delivery, ts
